$comment: Constants the Python package (apps/protspace) and the web app (packages/) must agree on.
Edit this file, run `pnpm shared-constants`, and commit it with the two modules it
generates; never edit those by hand. See contracts/README.md for what belongs here.

doc: Strings that mean "this annotation value is missing". A cell is missing
when it is null, a non-finite number, blank, or, trimmed and lower-cased,
one of these: `normalizeMissingValue` in the web, `is_missing_value` in
Python. That rule is code on each side, so the bundle contract suite runs
both on the same probe spellings.
`__na__` reserves the spelling of NA_VALUE: the bundle writer drops that
token unconditionally (it is the sentinel a missing cell carries), so a
genuine category literally spelled `__NA__` would be silently deleted on
export. Reading it as missing at ingestion makes the two agree.
Internal key of the N/A category: the legend value a missing cell gets,
and the key its colour and shape are saved under in a bundle's settings.
Never displayed; the web shows it as `N/A`.
Default swatch colour of the N/A category, which a saved category colour
overrides (categorical annotations only). Python gives a pinned N/A this
colour, so a CLI-styled legend matches the web's default.
Kelly's 21 colours of maximum contrast, in the order categories take them
(the category in slot i gets colour i). Medium gray (#848482) is left out:
it is reserved for special categories (Other, N/A). Very light and very
dark gray come last, for the least frequent categories. In order: vivid
yellow, strong purple, vivid orange, very light blue, vivid red, grayish
yellow, vivid green, strong purplish pink, strong blue, strong yellowish
pink, strong violet, vivid orange yellow, strong purplish red, vivid
greenish yellow, strong reddish brown, vivid yellowish green, deep
yellowish brown, vivid reddish orange, dark olive green, very light gray,
very dark gray.
Reference: Kelly, Kenneth L. Twenty-two colors of maximum contrast.
Color Engineering 3.26-27 (1965).
Palettes for categorical annotations: the only ids a bundle's
`selectedPaletteId` may name. `protspace style` warns on any other id, and
the web draws a gradient or unknown id with `kellys`. The web's
`COLOR_SCHEMES` holds the colours and must list exactly these ids plus
GRADIENT_PALETTE_IDS (the type check fails otherwise). A new palette also
goes in docs/guide/styling.md (Color palettes).
Sequential palettes for numeric annotations, chosen in the web's numeric
legend settings rather than through `selectedPaletteId`.
The gradient a numeric annotation starts on; one of GRADIENT_PALETTE_IDS.
Shapes a category can be drawn with: the `shape` values a bundle's
settings may hold. The web's `PointShape` type is exactly these.
Labels of an Arrow `bool` annotation column, false then true. Lower case,
as the browser has always shown one (`String(true)`), so legend colours
saved against a v2 bundle keep matching. Both v3 writers store a bool
column under these labels, and the web's writer keeps `sourceType: bool`
only while every label is one of them. Not Python's CANONICAL_BOOLEANS
(`False`/`True`), which are string cells the pipeline writes itself.
